concepts.def: Timber from broadleaf trees (oak, beech, mahogany); generally dense and slow-growing.
Timber from coniferous trees (pine, spruce); fast-growing and cheaper.
Engineered wood (MDF, plywood, chipboard); uniform sheets without grain direction.
Drying timber to reduce moisture content; air or kiln seasoning.
Direction of wood fibres; affects strength, appearance and machining.
Medium-Density Fibreboard: smooth-surfaced sheet ideal for painting and machining.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Materials & Their Working Properties — a core area of GCSE Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Materials & Their Working Properties brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Materials & Their Working Properties.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
